page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors operating at 2.8 GHz across 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4 GB per physical core. The CPU configuration features 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is present via hardware AES instructions. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, but it supplies a high-capacity baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation shows exceptional parallel computing capabilities alongside substantial memory throughput. In multi-threaded testing, the instance registers top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core scoring and Clang software compilation benchmarks, supplemented by strong stress-ng multi-core throughput. Memory subsystems demonstrate high bandwidth, reaching 480.5 GB/sec in uncached read operations and 235.58 GB/sec in write operations. Single-threaded metrics, including single-core Geekbench and compression tasks, remain within average tiers, reflecting consistent single-thread IPC rather than peak burst clocks. High network capacity and memory speed contribute to top-tier outcomes in Redis SET throughput and static web-serving volume.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton-based ARM architecture delivers high parallel compute density and substantial network throughput per allocated resource. Because the system contains no bundled local disks, persistence relies entirely on network-attached block storage, which must be factored into storage architectural design. The server is well matched for horizontally scalable microservices, high-concurrency static web serving, Clang compilation pipelines, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, and distributed relational database workloads requiring extensive memory bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz and 256 GB of system memory, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the AWS Nitro system, it delivers 200 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes hardware AES support. The instance includes no onboard local storage or discrete graphics accelerators. In synthetic and application benchmarks, m8gn.16xlarge excels in multi-threaded computation, Clang software builds, Redis throughput, and memory bandwidth, reaching 480.5 GB/sec on large read blocks. Single-threaded performance lands in the middle tier. By utilizing dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, the instance provides predictable performance efficiency for concurrent operations. The hardware layout is best matched for high-traffic web serving, memory-intensive caching clusters, large-scale software compilation, and scalable database engines operating across fast network interconnects.
